Therefore, it is recommended that testing not be performed and diagnosis be based on the presence of the EM rash.**”

Antibody testing can mislead in two ways described in the article:

So, blood testing is often unnecessary when EM + tick exposure are present (because antibodies may not yet exist), and antibody tests can mislead both early (not yet detectable antibodies) and when used alone (antibodies may reflect past exposure or background prevalence rather than current active disease).
